facts.fact: The National Population Commission launched VitalReg as a nationwide digital registration system for births and deaths under its electronic civil registration and vital statistics initiative, operational from 1 July 2026, on the account of its federal commissioner for Anambra.

VitalReg became operational across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory on 1 July 2026, replacing paper-based registration, according to the National Population Commission's federal commissioner and state director in Anambra.

The Commission's federal commissioner for Anambra describes VitalReg as an online platform with 24-hour access, digital certificate issuance and a secure national civil registration database, to which registration moves from paper; he does not describe the entry at a centre.

The National Population Commission says it operates 4,011 registration centres across the 774 local government areas, 131 of them in Anambra's 21, and plans about 8,000; the document says the platform is operational in every state but not how many of the centres enter on it. Undated, so the publication date is used.

The National Population Commission launched VitalReg and runs the registration centres, working with ALGON, NIMC, UNICEF and Barnksforte Technologies Ltd., on its federal commissioner's account of 1 July 2026's rollout.

The Commission's federal commissioner for Anambra says the platform is operated under a public-private partnership with Barnksforte Technologies Ltd., for system reliability, cybersecurity and continuing upgrades; undated, so the publication date is used.

systems.owner: National Population Commission (NPC); operated under a public-private partnership with Barnksforte Technologies Ltd.
systems.tiers: all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory; 4,011 NPC registration centres across 774 local government areas, about 8,000 planned
